title: Software Engineering Fundamentals Roadmap
description: A curated, stage-by-stage path from how computers and the web work, through object-oriented programming, to the behavioral and general interview skills every role needs.
audience: True beginners starting from zero, and self-taught developers who want to fill in the conceptual gaps formal education usually covers.
intro: This is the foundation the other roadmaps assume. If you have never written code, start here — the time invested pays back in every specialization you choose later.

stages.title: Programming, Computer & Web Foundations
stages.description: How computers actually run programs, what the web is, and the mental models that make every later topic less mysterious. No prior experience needed.
stages.milestone: You can explain what happens when you open a website, what an interpreter does, and write a simple program that manipulates data step by step.

steps.note: Take this slowly and do every exercise — this stage determines how easy everything after it feels.

stages.title: Object-Oriented Programming
stages.description: Classes, objects, inheritance, polymorphism, encapsulation — the modeling vocabulary used by C#, Java, and most enterprise codebases.
stages.milestone: You can model a small real-world system with classes and explain why each design decision was made, not just produce compiling code.

steps.note: Focus on the 'why' of each pillar — interviewers probe understanding, not definitions.

stages.title: General & Behavioral Interviews
stages.description: Technical skill gets you the interview; communication and self-awareness get you the offer. Learn the structures that make your answers land.
stages.milestone: You can answer common screening questions and tell a clear STAR story about a real project you worked on.

steps.note: Prepare two or three real stories now — you will reuse them in every interview loop.

stages.title: Growing Into Senior Engineering
stages.description: The skills that separate senior engineers from productive ones: technical judgment, decision-making under uncertainty, and owning outcomes beyond your own code.
stages.milestone: You can evaluate a technical decision with trade-offs, assess risk, and communicate the reasoning to both engineers and stakeholders.

steps.note: Return to this roadmap after some real project experience — the lessons hit differently with scars.
